name: request-response
title: Request/response
summary: Four concurrent small requests with asynchronous 1–4 KiB resource responses over four pre-established links.
description: Four concurrent request/reply round trips use four pre-established links at the manifest-owned standard 500-byte RNS MTU. Deterministic 32–128 byte requests remain below the link MDU, while deterministic 1–4 KiB responses unambiguously use the documented asynchronous resource-response path on both stacks. That preserves realistic small requests and gives each requester time to register its public receipt before the response resource can complete, without sleeps, blocking handlers, private queue inspection, reference mutation, or latency shims. Requests per second is the primary comparison; fractional-millisecond p50 and p99 wall-clock RTT run from request issue through complete response settlement.
conformance: Exactly four request lanes remain occupied at a 500-byte link MTU; sent == delivered == served, expected_response_bytes == response_bytes == served_response_bytes, and timeouts == raced == 0.
